+ # One Word API - Setup Guide
+ 
+ This guide will help you set up the One Word API development environment on your local machine.
+ 
+ ## Project Overview
+ 
+ One Word API is a Node.js backend service that powers the One Word application. It uses:
+ 
+ - **Node.js** with **Express** for the server
+ - **TypeScript** for type safety
+ - **Prisma** as an ORM for database interactions
+ - **PostgreSQL** database (via Docker)
+ - **Socket.IO** for real-time communications
+ - **JWT** for authentication
+ 
+ ## Prerequisites
+ 
+ Before you begin, make sure you have the following installed:
+ 
+ - **Node.js**: Version 16 or higher
+   - Download from [Node.js official website](https://nodejs.org/)
+   - Verify installation: `node --version`
+ 
+ - **Yarn**: Package manager
+   - Install with: `npm install -g yarn`
+   - Verify installation: `yarn --version`
+ 
+ - **Docker**: For running PostgreSQL locally
+   - Download from [Docker's official website](https://www.docker.com/get-started)
+   - Verify installation: `docker --version`
+ 
+ - **Git**: For cloning the repository
+   - Download from [Git official website](https://git-scm.com/downloads)
+   - Verify installation: `git --version`
+ 
+ ## Step 1: Clone the Repository
+ 
+ ```bash
+ git clone https://github.com/mariobrusarosco/api-one-word.git
+ cd api-one-word
+ ```
+ 
+ ## Step 2: Install Dependencies
+ 
+ Install all required dependencies using yarn:
+ 
+ ```bash
+ yarn
+ ```
+ 
+ ## Step 3: Set Up the Database
+ 
+ 1. Start the PostgreSQL container using Docker Compose:
+ 
+ ```bash
+ docker-compose up -d
+ ```
+ 
+ This will create and start a PostgreSQL container with the following credentials:
+ - User: postgres
+ - Password: postgres
+ - Database: postgres
+ - Port: 5432
+ 
+ 2. Verify that the container is running:
+ 
+ ```bash
+ docker ps
+ ```
+ 
+ You should see a container named `postgres_db` in the list.
+ 
+ ## Step 4: Set Up Environment Variables
+ 
+ 1. Create a `.env` file in the root directory by copying the example file:
+ 
+ ```bash
+ cp .example.env .env
+ ```
+ 
+ 2. The default values in the `.env` file should work for a local development environment, but you can customize them if needed:
+ 
+ ```
+ DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres
+ API_VERSION=/api/v1
+ MEMBER_PUBLIC_ID_COOKIE=memberId
+ JWT_SECRET=mysecretkey
+ ACCESS_CONTROL_ALLOW_ORIGIN=http://localhost:5173
+ NODE_ENV=development
+ OKTA_AUTH_COOKIE_NAME=oktaAuth
+ DEMO_MEMBER_ID=1
+ ```
+ 
+ ## Step 5: Set Up the Database Schema
+ 
+ 1. Generate the Prisma client:
+ 
+ ```bash
+ yarn generate-schema
+ ```
+ 
+ 2. Push the database schema to your local PostgreSQL instance:
+ 
+ ```bash
+ yarn db:push
+ ```
+ 
+ 3. (Optional) Seed the database with initial data:
+ 
+ ```bash
+ yarn seed
+ ```
+ 
+ ## Step 6: Start the Development Server
+ 
+ Start the development server with auto-reloading:
+ 
+ ```bash
+ yarn dev
+ ```
+ 
+ The API will be accessible at http://localhost:3000.
+ 
+ ## Step 7: Testing the Setup
+ 
+ ### REST API
+ You can test that the API is working correctly by accessing:
+ - http://localhost:3000/api/v1/health (should return a 200 OK status)
+ 
+ ### Socket Connection
+ You can test the Socket.IO connection by opening:
+ - http://localhost:3000/socket.html
+ 
+ ## Additional Commands
+ 
+ - **Start Prisma Studio** (database GUI):
+   ```bash
+   yarn studio
+   ```
+   This will start a web interface at http://localhost:5555 where you can browse and edit your database.
+ 
+ - **Run database migrations**:
+   ```bash
+   yarn db:migrate
+   ```
+ 
+ - **Build for production**:
+   ```bash
+   yarn build
+   ```
+ 
+ - **Start production server**:
+   ```bash
+   yarn start
+   ```
+ 
+ ## Troubleshooting
+ 
+ ### Database Connection Issues
+ - Ensure Docker is running
+ - Check if the PostgreSQL container is up with `docker ps`
+ - Verify the DATABASE_URL in your .env file matches the Docker setup
+ 
+ ### Application Won't Start
+ - Check if all dependencies are installed with `yarn`
+ - Ensure all environment variables are set correctly
+ - Make sure the required ports (3000, 5432) are not in use by other applications
+ 
+ ### Prisma Issues
+ - Try regenerating the Prisma client with `yarn generate-schema`
+ - For schema sync issues, run `yarn db:push` again
+ 
+ ## Next Steps
+ 
+ Once your local environment is set up, you might want to:
+ 
+ 1. Explore the API documentation in the Postman collection
+ 2. Check out the existing models in the Prisma schema
+ 3. Understand the Socket.IO implementation for real-time features
+ 
+ ## Resources
+ 
+ - [Project Repository](https://github.com/mariobrusarosco/api-one-word)
+ - [Postman Documentation](https://www.postman.com/mario-brusarosco/workspace/mario-brusarosco/collection/2930329-c069887a-c13d-4bee-8bda-e69e3f5b9163)
+ - [Sentry Dashboard](https://mario-79.sentry.io/issues/?project=4506356576747520&referrer=sidebar&statsPeriod=30d)
+ - [Hosted API](https://api-one-word.mariobrusarosco.com/)
+ 
```

---

Yes, the error occurs because port 5432 is already in use by another PostgreSQL container or service on your system, as shown in your screenshot.

You can easily change the port by modifying your docker-compose.yml file. Here's how:

1. Edit the `docker-compose.yml` file:

---

```diff
        POSTGRES_DB: postgres  # This is the default database to create
      ports:
-       - "5432:5432"
+       - "5433:5432"
      volumes:
        - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

---

2. Now you also need to update your `.env` file to use the new port:

---

```diff
- DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/postgres
+ DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5433/postgres
  API_VERSION=/api/v1
  MEMBER_PUBLIC_ID_COOKIE=memberId
```

---

Now you can start your containers with:

```bash
docker-compose up -d
```

This configuration:
1. Maps PostgreSQL's internal port 5432 to external port 5433 on your host machine
2. Updates the connection string to use port 5433 when connecting to the database

The database will still run on its default port (5432) inside the container, but you'll access it through port 5433 on your host machine.

+ /**
+  * Notifies all participants in a game room that a participant has exited
+  * @param socketServer - The Socket.IO server instance
+  * @param gameId - The game room ID
+  * @param user - The user who exited the game
+  */
+ export const notifyParticipantExit = async (
+   socketServer: any,
+   gameId: string,
+   user: { userID: string; username: string }
+ ) => {
+   // Get updated list of participants (excluding the one who left)
+   const remainingUsers = await getSocketsFromRoom(socketServer, gameId);
+   
+   // Emit participant exit event to all users in the room
+   socketServer.in(gameId).emit(
+     SocketEvents.PARTICIPANT_EXIT, 
+     { 
+       user,
+       message: `${user.username} has left the game`,
+       timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
+     }
+   );
+   
+   // Update the participant list for all remaining users
+   socketServer.in(gameId).emit(
+     SocketEvents.UPDATE_GAME_ROOM_PARTICIPANTS, 
+     remainingUsers
+   );
+   
+   return remainingUsers;
+ } 
```

Now that we've implemented the participant exit notification system, let's create a quick documentation for it:

---

```diff
- 
+ # Participant Exit Notification System
+ 
+ ## Overview
+ 
+ This document describes how the One Word API notifies game participants when another participant exits a game, either by explicitly leaving or disconnecting.
+ 
+ ## Implementation
+ 
+ The system uses Socket.IO to provide real-time notifications to all participants in a game when someone leaves. This happens in two scenarios:
+ 
+ 1. **Explicit Exit**: When a user intentionally leaves a game (e.g., clicks a "Leave Game" button)
+ 2. **Disconnection**: When a user disconnects from the Socket.IO server (e.g., closes the browser)
+ 
+ ## Events
+ 
+ ### Client-side Events (to listen for)
+ 
+ - `participant-exit`: Emitted when a participant leaves a game
+   - Payload:
+     ```typescript
+     {
+       user: {
+         userID: string;
+         username: string;
+       },
+       message: string; // e.g., "Username has left the game"
+       timestamp: string; // ISO date string
+     }
+     ```
+ 
+ - `update-game-room-participants`: Emitted after a participant exits to provide the updated list of participants
+   - Payload: Array of user objects
+     ```typescript
+     [
+       {
+         userID: string;
+         username: string;
+       },
+       // ...more participants
+     ]
+     ```
+ 
+ ### Client-side Events (to emit)
+ 
+ - `leave-game-room`: To explicitly leave a game room
+   - Payload: `gameId` (string)
+ 
+ ## Frontend Implementation Example
+ 
+ ```typescript
+ // Example of how to use these events in the frontend
+ socket.on('participant-exit', (data) => {
+   console.log(`${data.user.username} has left the game`);
+   // Show a notification to the user
+   showNotification(data.message);
+   
+   // You could also play a sound, update UI, etc.
+ });
+ 
+ socket.on('update-game-room-participants', (participants) => {
+   // Update the list of participants in the UI
+   updateParticipantsList(participants);
+ });
+ 
+ // To leave a game
+ function leaveGame(gameId) {
+   socket.emit('leave-game-room', gameId);
+   // Navigate away from the game page or update UI as needed
+ }
+ ```
+ 
+ ## Server-side Implementation
+ 
+ The server handles participant exits by:
+ 
+ 1. Detecting when a user leaves a game room (either explicitly or by disconnection)
+ 2. Getting the updated list of participants
+ 3. Notifying all remaining participants with the participant-exit event
+ 4. Updating the participant list for all remaining users
+ 
+ This provides a seamless experience where all participants are immediately aware when someone leaves the game. 
```

I've implemented a complete solution to notify other game participants when someone exits. Here's what I did:

1. Added a new `PARTICIPANT_EXIT` event in the SocketEvents enum
2. Created a `notifyParticipantExit` utility function that:
   - Gets the updated list of participants (excluding the one who left)
   - Emits a detailed exit notification to all remaining participants
   - Updates the participant list for everyone

3. Enhanced the GameSocket class with:
   - Updated `leaveGameRoom` method to use the new notification system for disconnections
   - Added a new `handleExplicitExit` method that processes explicit leave requests
   - Added the new handler to the setup process

4. Improved the SocketController's disconnect handler with additional logging

5. Created documentation for the participant exit notification system

The system now handles both scenarios:
- When a user explicitly leaves a game (via UI interaction)
- When a user disconnects unexpectedly (closes browser, loses connection)

Other participants will receive a notification with details about who left and when, making the gaming experience more transparent and informative.

Let's simplify our approach and create a documentation file to explain how to implement participant exit notifications on the frontend:

---

```diff
- 
+ # Implementing Participant Exit Notifications
+ 
+ This document explains how we've implemented the toast notifications that appear when a participant exits a game.
+ 
+ ## Overview
+ 
+ When a participant leaves a game (either by explicitly leaving or disconnecting), the server sends a `game-participant-exit` event to all remaining participants. The frontend listens for this event and displays a toast notification.
+ 
+ ## Implementation Details
+ 
+ ### 1. Socket Event Handling
+ 
+ The participant exit events are handled in the `useGameSocket` hook:
+ 
+ ```typescript
+ // src/domains/games/hooks/use-game-socket.ts
+ const watchForParticipantExits = useCallback(() => {
+   tableId && on<IGameParticipantExitPayload>(
+     SocketEvents.GAME_PARTICIPANT_EXIT,
+     (exitData) => {
+       // Show toast notification with custom styling
+       toast({
+         title: "Participant Left",
+         description: exitData.message,
+         variant: "destructive",
+         duration: 5000,
+       });
+     }
+   );
+ }, [tableId, on, toast]);
+ ```
+ 
+ ### 2. Toast Notification System
+ 
+ We're using the app's toast notification system powered by the `useToast` hook from our UI system. The toast component is already included in the app's root layout.
+ 
+ ### 3. Event Structure
+ 
+ The participant exit event payload has the following structure:
+ 
+ ```typescript
+ interface IGameParticipantExitPayload {
+   user: {
+     userID: string;
+     username: string;
+   };
+   message: string; // e.g., "Username has left the game"
+   timestamp: string; // ISO date string
+ }
+ ```
+ 
+ ## Testing
+ 
+ To test the participant exit notifications:
+ 
+ 1. Start the API server: `yarn dev` in the api-one-word directory
+ 2. Start the frontend: `yarn dev` in the one-word directory
+ 3. Open two browser windows and log in with different accounts
+ 4. Both users should join the same game
+ 5. Have one user leave the game by either:
+    - Clicking a "Leave Game" button
+    - Closing their browser tab
+ 6. The remaining user should see a toast notification saying "[Username] has left the game"
+ 
+ ## Customization
+ 
+ ### Styling the Toast
+ 
+ You can customize the appearance of the toast by modifying the `toast` call:
+ 
+ ```typescript
+ toast({
+   title: "Custom Title",
+   description: exitData.message,
+   variant: "default", // or "destructive" for error-styled toast
+   duration: 3000, // duration in milliseconds
+ });
+ ```
+ 
+ ### Adding Sound Effects
+ 
+ If you want to add sound effects when a participant leaves:
+ 
+ ```typescript
+ // Play a sound when a participant exits
+ const audio = new Audio('/sounds/participant-exit.mp3');
+ audio.volume = 0.5;
+ audio.play().catch(() => {
+   // Handle errors if sound can't be played
+ });
+ ```
+ 
+ Make sure to add the sound file to the public directory.
+ 
+ ## Future Enhancements
+ 
+ Potential future enhancements could include:
+ 
+ 1. Customized toast appearance based on the participant's role or status
+ 2. Different notifications for explicit exits vs. disconnections
+ 3. Persistent history of participant joins/exits in a game session 
```
